$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=-3 \\ y &=5 \\ z &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=5$ and $z=-6$ into the first equation, we get

$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.
